reviews.title: Extremely disappointed
reviews.text:
This app only tracks your workout if you manually open it, which is ridiculous for something that’s supposed to run automatically. I was in a 30-day challenge with money on the line, and I was winning the entire time. On the very last day, I forgot to open the app, even though I DID the workout and surprise: it wasn’t counted.
I “lost” the challenge and lost actual money, despite having completed everything.
This isn’t just frustrating, it’s unfair. An app that costs money and promotes challenges should not punish users for something so small, especially when there’s proof the workout was done. If you’re joining challenges, be warned: one forgotten tap can cost you the win.
Do better.

reviews.title: Great Accountability App with Tons of Potential
reviews.text:
This is exactly what I’ve been looking for and I have enjoyed using the GymRats app. I think it has so much potential! One of the best features is the check-in system, which makes it easy to keep your group accountable. It’s also a great way to stay connected with friends and coworkers who can’t physically work out with you but still want to stay on track together. Syncing workouts from your Apple health is super easy and the photo upload feature really ties everything together.

That said, I do think the app could benefit from a few improvements. First, the name is a bit cringey and doesn’t fully reflect what the app offers—I probably would have found it sooner if it had a name that better conveyed its purpose.

As for features, I’d love to see:
•Expanded chat capabilities, similar to Discord or Slack, where users can react to posts and create threads/ pin posts.
•Personal weight loss goals and weight loss focused competitions to keep users motivated.
•Nutrition or meal post features to complement fitness progress.
•Profile upgrades, including fitness goals, a bio section, highlights, and photos to personalize the experience.
•A streak system to encourage consistency and reward regular check-ins.
•The ability to share the leaderboard on socials would also be a great option.

Overall, GymRats is a fantastic tool for accountability, and I’m excited to see how it evolves! Looking forward to future updates.

reviews.title: Open points?
reviews.text: My friends and I use this all the time for group challenges. But, it looks like you got rid of open point style challenges. One challenge we like to do is pick you poison, where each lady picks four possible points a day to get. We all pick our own four points at the beginning of the month and use this ap to track them. It is really fun. But for June, it looks like there is no more open point option. There are these new hustle points, which look super fun for later, but they won’t work for open points. We have also used open points for other challenges where the group says what the points equate to rather than the ap telling us. Please bring back open point tracking.

reviews.title: Easy, simple, and fun
reviews.text:
This is perfect!! I love how customizable this is. My friend and I are working out together but hated apps that made you weigh yourself and count calories. We just want to focus on moving and enjoying fitness, not worrying so much about obsessing over macros. We’ve been using this 3 weeks so far and it’s super motivating! I wish you could edit the photo after the workout is posted, though. It would also be nice to see the progress total—such as total number of minutes or distance or whatever goal it is. I’d love an option with a progress bar or percentage showing how far into the challenge you are too. 

Either way—it’s nice there’s different options like hustle points, which we’re going to try next. PS for those who do want to track calories burned, you can have that option. It also has distance, time, and some other options, too! This is a great app.

reviews.title: BEST app find for fitness with friends!!
reviews.text:
Can’t thank you enough for this simple, easy to use, fun and most excellent app. It’s EXACTLY what I hoped to find. 

A small group of friends and I did a ‘mileage’ challenge last year someone found online. The upside was since we were in it together it made a HUGE difference in everyone’s commitment to get more fit. Downsides: It was pricey for everyone and fairly clunky to even log miles…but the worst was since it was based on miles-only it really left out some friends who wanted to participate and were working out religiously in cardio or yoga classes but not getting mileage. 

The super simple design was vital to get everyone in our group to download and learn a new thing. But it’s so fast and easy we did it. 

But the flexibility of your app is the best feature! We set up our January challenge to be based on workout minutes instead of miles. That is really allowing ALL fitness levels to participate and feel good about their progress—as we have everyone from serious distance runners to those with physical disabilities in our dozen or so participants. 

At first I was bummed that it didn’t offer an option to connect our Fitbits and Strava etc. But as we all started using the option of posting a photo from the workout — that has become its own joy to see out of state friends on their yoga mats or a pic from their run. We love that and it’s bringing us closer as friends and helping grow fitness routines. THANK YOU!!! Boring auto posting from our watches etc would feel so impersonal now! 

I would happily pay for this app in the future even without additional features being added. 

**Sure hope you offer an option where I could pay one fee for my group of X people (12ish would be my wish) so that it would be free to those I invite.**

It would have been MUCH harder to get everyone on if they had to pay individually even if the price were low. Just a mental hurdle for some of the less techy among us or those on the fence about joining in or in a hard $ spot. 

Thank you again. It is growing our fitness and friendships. THAT is value!! 

Ps I could see you adapting this format to other groups of friends/family who want to commit to a practice of some kind — from makers who want to dedicate more minutes to their craft and share pics of the process…to a group of book lovers who want to read a certain number of books and want to post and say a little about the book they just finished. Keep up the great work!!
